title: Human activity helped make 2025 third-hottest year on record, experts say — The Guardian
text: The unnatural heat is largely the result of a blanket of carbon pollution smothering the Earth, worsening most weather extremes and jeopardising the stable conditions in which humanity has thrived. Copernicus found temperatures over the tropical Atlantic and Indian Ocean were less extreme in 2025 than in 2024, but these were offset partly by higher temperatures at the poles. Antarctica recorded its hottest year, and the Arctic its second-hottest. Polar sea ice cover fell to its lowest level since satellite observations began in the 1970s in February. Over the year as a whole, half of the planet’s land experienced more days than average with at least “strong” heat stress, when temperatures feel above 32C.
